extracted.intended_audience: scientists, research-integrity advocates, and readers following allegations of scientific misconduct (Retraction Watch/blog readership)
extracted.subtask_description: A comment-thread on a blog post discussing alleged image manipulation, retractions, investigations, and community reactions to an individual researcher's large set of suspect publications. The thread includes calls for investigations, debate about due process, and suggestions for community policing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image manipulation indicates research misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Some of the evidence disclosed so far are obvious manipulation of data, indicating serious research misconducts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers point to duplicated or altered images across many papers as strong evidence; multiple commenters note that manipulated images are 'obvious' and have prompted retractions. Example: links to discovered manipulated figures and retraction notices (e.g., PubMed/NCBI links) and blog reports (Abnormal Science, JuiichiJigen).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of primary/raw data as proof of authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Send the PRIMARY raw data and your analysis report to ORI to stop the investigation against BBA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability of primary/raw data and underlying analysis is presented as a definitive way to demonstrate which papers are genuine; commenters urge submission of raw data to ORI/institutions as part of resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional/ORI investigation and due process
rubrics_metrics.description: Let's wait for the decision of ORI/MDACC; 'innocent until proven guilty' and institutions should give final verdicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Debate in the thread balances calls for immediate public sanctioning vs. waiting for formal institutional/ORI processes. Commenters note investigations can be long and involve many papers and people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough investigation should include coauthors and collaborators
rubrics_metrics.description: Proper investigation means most of the coauthors (with significant number of papers as co-authors) and prominent collaborators should also be investigated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several commenters argue that scrutiny should extend beyond the PI to collaborators/coauthors who appear across multiple suspect papers, to identify systemic problems and 'collateral damage.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction as a journal-level indicator of misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Cancer Letters had already given an opinion on BBA’s misconducts by retracting his ‘accepted’ article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journal retractions (and lists of retractions on sites like Retraction Watch) are treated as formal signals that the literature has been corrected and as evidence supporting allegations; commenters track and list retractions as milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility (non-reproducibility) as a red flag
rubrics_metrics.description: Non reproducibility of his data was pointed out previously and is a concerning sign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters reference prior failures of other groups to reproduce results as further evidence of problems; reproducibility concerns can precede image analysis and retractions and motivate scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI responsibility and oversight (lab recordkeeping)
rubrics_metrics.description: If he signs everybody lab book, he should have seen all the data on daily basis… then why does he blame his postdocs for mistakes in these 65 papers… he is solely responsible or not sharp enough to catch the errors/mistakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signatures on lab notebooks and supervisory practices are discussed as indicators of PI oversight (or lack thereof). Signing blank notebooks is criticized as poor practice that undermines accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use forensic image analysis/software to detect duplications
rubrics_metrics.description: JuiichiJigen/Abnormal Science blogs and their software have been used to uncover duplicated/manipulated figures across many papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters recommend running suspect papers through image-scanning tools and sharing results with investigative blogs and institutions; forensic tools are presented as effective community instruments for discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review and editorial responsibility to detect obvious flaws
rubrics_metrics.description: Why not some-one find out who were the reviewers of all his 65 papers? Generally if the reviewer is concerned - he/she gives proper attention to minute details - some of the image needs only one glance to understand the flaws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters argue that reviewers and editors should catch obvious image problems and that journals bear responsibility. Calls are made for reviewer accountability and transparency from journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of reviewer identities increases accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the journal has the policy to disclose reviewer names we will not be able to find out; some journals (biomedcentral/frontiers) do interactive reviewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested remedy: journals that disclose reviewer identities or use interactive review can improve accountability and detection of problematic papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public disclosure and media coverage as a protective mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Public awareness of what is going on will possibly save someone from committing to the lab while MDACC decides on course of action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters advocate spreading the story (e.g., to Indian newspapers) to warn potential job-seekers and to increase pressure for timely institutional action. Tension exists between publicizing allegations and preserving due process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and honors may need reassessment pending findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there any policy to retract awards? (e.g., an award being presented despite allegations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion about whether awarding bodies should pause or revoke honors when recipients are under credible allegation; debate about whether an award for a book vs. scientific research should be treated differently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication/coauthorship patterns as indicators of suspicious productivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables/lists of number of publications with BBA and suspected duplications among coauthors suggest suspicious prolific collaborators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters compile publication counts and coauthorship networks to identify patterns that may merit closer scrutiny (e.g., very high output from particular collaborators).

rubrics_metrics.name: Downstream consequences for patents and fields built on flawed work
rubrics_metrics.description: I wonder what happens to patents that have been issued if the underlying research is proven to be 'flawed' and the papers are retracted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters raise concerns about the legal and scientific consequences when foundational studies are invalidated—patents, further research, and funding built on suspect results may be affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding ad hominem / racist commentary; focus on root causes
rubrics_metrics.description: Some of these comments also sound entirely racist… hardly appropriate for people claiming to be self righteous! It doesn’t matter where you come from and where you have worked – as long as you do good and honest research work – everything falls safe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several commenters call for focusing on misconduct and systemic causes rather than on nationality or personal attacks; maintain constructive, non-discriminatory discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community monitoring/whistleblowing as valid oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: I have uncovered another 14 papers from 2003-2005 with manipulated images. Files have been sent to Abnormal Science and JuiichiJigen blogs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bloggers, whistleblowers, and independent watchdogs are portrayed as effective at uncovering widespread problems; community-sourced evidence and sharing with investigative outlets are recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional remedies (lab closure, firing, prosecution) vs. restraint
rubrics_metrics.description: There is only one remedy for this whole situation… BBA lab should immediately be sealed and closed…and BBA himself should go to Himalaya… or he should be fired/prosecuted publicly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commenters demand strict institutional sanctions (closure, firing, prosecution), while others caution about waiting for formal findings; this represents competing views on proportional institutional responses.
